title: Investigate tiered burst failsafe causing reserved-pool headroom undershoot
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported elevated 429/503 throttling and sustained latency spikes during multi-tenant bursts. Investigation shows the tiered 'burst failsafe' logic sometimes reduces reserved-pool headroom too aggressively when multiple burst signals overlap across tenants and when allocator telemetry is delayed. The result: autoscaler and allocator enter a transient oscillation where slots are not provisioned quickly enough, causing customer requests to be routed to lower-tier fallbacks or throttled.

Scope: Affects reserved pools backed by mixed instance types (spot + on-demand), primarily in eu-west-1 and us-central-1. Impacted tenants include FinSolve and MedoraPay (support cases #3421, #3459). Estimated customer request loss during peak minutes: 5-15% for affected pools.

Goals: 1) Stabilize production by deploying a targeted hotfix to the burst failsafe guardrails. 2) Add telemetry and an automated canary to detect headroom desync earlier. 3) Postmortem and longer-term improvements to autoscaler decision logic and allocator smoothing factors.
updates: 2026-03-05 — Detection: On-call alerted by increased 429 rates for several Dedicated tenants. Pager duty runbook executed; initial mitigation set routing fallback to model-variant:low-cost for affected customers.

2026-03-06 — Triage: Reproduced headroom undershoot in staging by simulating concurrent tenant bursts and artificially delaying allocator telemetry (instrumented test harness). Observed autoscaler decision flip-flop when failsafe TTL < allocator update interval.

2026-03-07 — Hypothesis: Failsafe aggressively clamps headroom when burst_count > threshold and allocator reports transient low free_slots; combination with telemetry smoothing factor (alpha=0.15) causes underestimation. Filed iterative experiment to tune alpha and TTL.

2026-03-08 — Mitigation: Deployed temporary config change to increase burst-failsafe TTL from 20s to 60s and raised headroom floor from 8% to 14% for eu-west-1/us-central-1. Immediate reduction in 429s observed (~70% improvement within 10m). Rollout tracked with metric dashboard: /dashboards/ops/autoscale/burst-headroom.

2026-03-09 — Hotfix PR: Implemented conservative headroom estimator guard and added a short-circuit that prevents simultaneous clamping when allocator update lag > 2x expected interval. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8382 — landed to canary (canary hosts 5% of traffic).

2026-03-10 — Canary results: No regressions in latency or cost observed at 5% traffic. One customer in canary experienced degraded throughput; traced to tenant-specific burst signature — reverted tenant routing for that customer and captured bloom of edge-case metrics.

2026-03-12 — Rollout: Gradual rollout to 50% then 100% of hosts in affected regions completed. Monitored for 72h window. Post-rollback verification runbook executed to ensure fail-open semantics preserved.

2026-03-13 — Monitoring: Added new alerting rule autoscale.headroom_desync.v1 to fire when headroom delta > 10% for > 30s and allocator_lag > 5s. Added dashboard panel for tenant-level burst_count correlation.

2026-03-14 — Follow-ups: Start on long-term work to replace hard TTLs with adaptive backoff, and to incorporate request-level priority and tenant burst budgets into autoscaler decisions. Plan for RFC and design review next cycle.
